question: What main chemical messengers does the endocrine system use to coordinate body functions?
explanation: The endocrine system uses hormones released directly into the bloodstream to reach and regulate distant target organs. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T3#BMP121_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why is keeping hormone levels within a steady range important for the body?

options.A: To stop external changes from affecting the skin
options.B: To make nervous system impulses travel faster
options.C: To maintain internal balance and prevent stress on the body
options.D: To prevent red blood cell production from stopping

explanation: Keeping hormone levels balanced protects the body from the harmful effects of having too much or too little of a specific chemical. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T3#BMP121_U4_T3_h1)

question: What is the main job of a negative feedback loop in the endocrine system?

options.A: To reverse a change and restore normal balance
options.B: To turn chemical signals into fast electrical impulses
options.C: To permanently stop hormone production in all glands
options.D: To amplify a stimulus until a physical event finishes

explanation: Negative feedback works by counteracting a change, bringing the internal environment back to its normal baseline. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T3#BMP121_U4_T3_h2)

question: What happens when a hormone level gets too high in a standard negative feedback system?

options.A: The nervous system takes over the gland completely
options.B: The gland is stimulated to produce even more hormone
options.C: Target organs stop responding to all chemical signals
options.D: Secretion of that hormone is slowed down to lower levels

explanation: High levels of a hormone signal the body to stop releasing more, keeping amounts safe and balanced. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T3#BMP121_U4_T3_h2)

question: Which of the following describes how a positive feedback loop works?

options.A: It turns slow hormonal signals into quick reflexes
options.B: It works to return a fluctuating variable to a steady set point
options.C: It blocks all communication between the brain and organs
options.D: It builds up the original stimulus to drive a process forward

explanation: Positive feedback builds on the initial change, pushing the system forward to complete a specific goal like childbirth. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T3#BMP121_U4_T3_h3)

question: Why does the body use positive feedback loops much less often than negative feedback loops?

options.A: Hormones in positive feedback cannot travel in the blood
options.B: Positive feedback only works during childhood
options.C: Unchecked positive feedback can cause dangerous runaway effects
options.D: Positive feedback requires too much nervous system energy

explanation: Because positive feedback keeps increasing a response, it needs a clear stopping point to avoid harming the body. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T3#BMP121_U4_T3_h3)

question: Which part of the brain releases hormones to control the anterior pituitary gland?
explanation: The hypothalamus produces control hormones that travel to the anterior pituitary to direct its releases. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T3#BMP121_U4_T3_h4)

question: What is the main benefit of having a multi-step pathway involving the hypothalamus, pituitary, and other glands?

options.A: To stop the brain from receiving signals from organs
options.B: To make hormone levels increase continuously without stopping
options.C: To skip the bloodstream and use direct nerve pathways
options.D: To allow precise control over circulating hormone levels

explanation: Having multiple checkpoints helps the body finely adjust and control hormone output with high accuracy. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T3#BMP121_U4_T3_h4)

question: A midwife gives synthetic oxytocin to strengthen weak contractions during labour. Which natural body process is this supporting?

options.A: A positive feedback loop involving cervical stretch and hormone release
options.B: A hypothalamic shutdown of the pituitary gland
options.C: A negative feedback loop that lowers blood pressure
options.D: A steady hormone release that ignores uterine stretching

explanation: Synthetic oxytocin helps the natural positive feedback loop where contractions stretch the cervix, releasing more natural oxytocin. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T3#BMP121_U4_T3_h5)

question: Why must midwives pay close attention to thyroid hormone levels in early pregnancy?

options.A: The thyroid stops responding to pituitary signals during pregnancy
options.B: Thyroid hormones work entirely through positive feedback during gestation
options.C: The developing baby relies on maternal thyroid hormones before its own gland works
options.D: Maternal thyroid levels drop to zero right after conception

explanation: Early baby development depends on the mother's thyroid hormones, making normal endocrine function vital for healthy growth. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T3#BMP121_U4_T3_h5)
